title: GitHub - firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server: Official Firecrawl MCP server, the context API for AI agents: search, scrape, and interact with the web, plus parse, crawl, map, Agent and Monitor, from any MCP client.
snippet:
# Firecrawl MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings [Firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl), the context API for AI agents, to MCP-compatible clients: search, scrape, and interact with the live web and get back clean Markdown or structured data.
> Big thanks to [@vrknetha](https://github.com/vrknetha), [@knacklabs](https://www.knacklabs.ai) for the initial implementation!
## Features
- Search the web, optionally with full page content for each result
- Search indexes for developer sources (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and docs), US government sources, and scientific papers (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)
- Look up a protein's curated subcellular location and function in UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, with the evidence and papers behind each statement
- Scrape any URL into clean Markdown
- Parse PDFs and documents
- Crawl a site for content from many pages, or map it to discover its URLs
- Interact with pages in a real browser: click, type, fill forms, and navigate dynamic pages
- Run Agent jobs for multi-source research that returns structured data
- Monitor pages and get notified when their content changes
- Check current and historical Firecrawl credit usage
- Automatic retries and rate limiting
- Cloud and self-hosted support
- SSE support
> Play around with [our MCP Server on MCP.so's playground](https://mcp.so/playground?server=firecrawl-mcp-server) or on [Klavis AI](https://www.klavis.ai/mcp-servers).

This server lists 34 tools when the full profile registers with default settings (feedback tools included, not running in local-keyless mode). Setting `FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1` and/or `FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1` removes the corresponding feedback tools and reduces this count, as does local keyless startup. For clients with a tool-slot limit: the hosted keyless endpoint (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`, no API key) exposes only 3 (`firecrawl_scrape`, `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_parse`), and the dedicated search-only endpoint (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-search`) exposes a fixed set of 12 tools (search, developer, government, and research search, Alexandria catalogue lookup and execution, people and company search and enrichment, and job postings).
## Installation
### Hosted MCP (keyless free tier)
Connect to the remote hosted server with no setup:
```
https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```

title: Get Started
Developers & MCP
snippet:
Firecrawl’s MCP server connects to Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other Model Context Protocol clients so your assistant can pull live documentation, discover site structures, and extract structured data on demand.
## Start with a Template
## MCP Server Firecrawl
Official MCP server - Search, scrape, and interact with the web from Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients
## Open Lovable
Build complete applications from any website instantly
**Get started with MCP in minutes.** Follow our [setup guide](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server#installation) to integrate Firecrawl into Claude Desktop or Cursor.
## How It Works
Integrate Firecrawl directly into your AI coding workflow through Model Context Protocol. Once configured, your AI assistant gains access to a set of Firecrawl web tools it can call on your behalf:
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Scrape** | Extract content or structured data from a single URL |
| **Batch Scrape** | Extract content from multiple known URLs in parallel |
| **Map** | Discover all indexed URLs on a website |
| **Crawl** | Walk a site section and extract content from every page |
| **Search** | Search the web and optionally extract content from results |

Currently, Claude Desktop and Cursor have native MCP support. More AI assistants are adding support regularly. You can also use the MCP SDK to build custom integrations.
Yes. VS Code supports MCP natively: run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and enter `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`. To add it by hand, put Firecrawl under `mcpServers` in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` for all your workspaces, or in `.mcp.json` at the workspace root to share it with your team:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"firecrawl": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp"
}
}
}
```

title: Agent Development Kit (ADK)
snippet:
Connect Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) to Firecrawl through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so your agents can search, scrape, crawl, and map the web for clean context.
## Overview
Firecrawl provides an MCP server that seamlessly integrates with Google’s ADK, enabling your agents to efficiently scrape, crawl, and extract structured data from any website. The integration supports both cloud-based and self-hosted Firecrawl instances with streamable HTTP for optimal performance.
## Features
- Efficient web scraping, crawling, and content discovery from any website
- Advanced search capabilities and intelligent content extraction
- Autonomous web research with the Firecrawl agent
- Browser interaction, file parsing, and change monitoring
- Flexible deployment (cloud-based or self-hosted)
- Optimized for modern web environments with streamable HTTP support
## Prerequisites
- Obtain an API key for Firecrawl from [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev)
- Install Google ADK with MCP support: `pip install "google-adk[mcp]"`
## Setup
```
import os
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent
from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.mcp_session_manager import StreamableHTTPConnectionParams
from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.mcp_toolset import MCPToolset
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY = os.environ["FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"]
root_agent = Agent(
model="gemini-3.8-flash",
name="firecrawl_agent",
description='A helpful assistant for scraping websites with Firecrawl',
instruction='Help the user search for website content',
tools=[
MCPToolset(
connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(
url="https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp",
headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {FIRECRAWL_API_KEY}"},
),
)
],
)
```
Set `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` in the environment that starts ADK. Do not put its value in agent prompts, source control, or the MCP URL. The local MCP package requires Node.js 22 or newer.
## Available Tools
| Tool | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Scrape Tool | `firecrawl_scrape` | Scrape content from a single URL, or extract structured data with a JSON format |
| Map Tool | `firecrawl_map` | Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site |
| Search Tool | `firecrawl_search` | Search the web and optionally extract content from search results |
| Crawl Tool | `firecrawl_crawl` | Crawl a site or section and return its pages |
| Check Crawl Status | `firecrawl_check_crawl_status` | Check the status of a crawl job |
| Parse Tool | `firecrawl_parse` | Extract content from a PDF, document, spreadshe

title: For Agents
snippet:
Keyless MCP is rate limited and exposes Search, Scrape, and Parse. Add an API key to unlock the full tool surface or higher limits.
## Add an API key
[Create a Firecrawl API key](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys), then add it as a bearer token on the same endpoint in your client config:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"firecrawl": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp",
"headers": {
"Authorization": "Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>"
}
}
}
}
```
In Droid, pass the key as a header and turn off OAuth:
```
droid mcp add firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp --type http \
--header "Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>" --no-oauth
```
To sign in through the browser instead of pasting a key, see [For Humans](/mcp-server/oauth). [Authentication](/authentication) compares API keys, MCP sign-in and OAuth for your own app.
## Verify your connection
Open your client’s MCP status or tool list and confirm that `firecrawl` is connected. A keyless connection shows `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_scrape`, and `firecrawl_parse`; an API-key connection can expose the [full tool surface](/mcp-server/tools), subject to plan, deployment, and team policy.

## Run locally
Start the open-source server over stdio or Streamable HTTP.
For the current keyless allowance and plan limits, see [Rate limits](/rate-limits#keyless-no-api-key).

title: MCP Web Search & Scrape in GitHub Copilot
snippet:
Connect [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli) or [Copilot in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/overview) to Firecrawl through the hosted MCP server, then sign in with your Firecrawl account. The Copilot coding agent connects with an API key. The server URLs below are client configuration values, not pages to open directly in a browser.
## Copilot CLI
### 1. Add Firecrawl
```
copilot mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth
```
This writes the server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. You can also run `/mcp add` inside an interactive session and choose the **HTTP** type, or edit the file directly:
~/.copilot/mcp-config.json
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"firecrawl": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth",
"tools": ["*"]
}
}
}
```
### 2. Sign in and verify
```
copilot
```
On the first connection, Copilot CLI opens the Firecrawl sign-in flow in your browser, where you choose a team and approve the connection. Enter `/mcp` to confirm that `firecrawl` is connected.
### Use an API key instead
For unattended use, [create a Firecrawl API key](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys), export it as `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, and add the API-key endpoint with a bearer header:
```
copilot mcp add --transport http \
--header "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" \
firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```
The key is stored in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, so keep that file out of source control.
## VS Code
### 1. Add Firecrawl
Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and pick **Copilot Global** as the destination. Or add the server yourself to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` (every workspace) or to `.mcp.json` at your workspace root (shared with your team):
~/.copilot/mcp-config.json
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"firecrawl": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth"
}
}
}
```
These portable files use a top-level `mcpServers` object.

```
copilot mcp add --transport http \
--header "Authorization: Bearer $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY" \
firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```
